text: Where can customers have the monthly coffee subscription delivered?
note: Answer is mostly exclusions (islands, Portugal); single-bag orders still ship there, which is the trap.

text: Is shipping on us for a newcomer's initial subscription parcel?
note: Free only while the courier keeps the old per-parcel rate; the rate was never confirmed in the corpus.

text: Has Lucía signed off on the actual wording of the welcome email?
note: She approved the plan's section structure only; copy approval never appears and the email went out as drafted.

text: Who OK'd the higher Instagram spend for the final week of September, and how much was it?
note: Approval is a bare 'sounds good' reply to the request that carries the amount.

text: Are we running the joint prize draw with the neighbourhood bread shop?
note: Proposed, liked, postponed; never accepted or declined.

text: What does the Club cost per month?
note: Owner insists on one price, co-founder told the developer another (in Russian); still open at corpus end.

text: What perk do people get for joining the mailing list at launch?
note: Kickoff discount code replaced by a free sample nine days later; the doc's email draft still shows the code.

text: When did Daniel at the box manufacturer dispatch the printed mailers?
note: Two authors named Daniel in one chat; the ops Daniel's subscriber-shipping date is the trap, plus a superseded earlier aim.

text: What return on ad spend did the September Instagram campaign achieve?
note: No figure exists; CTR, CPC and reach numbers are distractors.

text: Почему в сентябре Андрей перевёл магазин на другой платёжный сервис?
note: False premise: switching was proposed and explicitly declined.

text: How old can the beans be, at most, when an order leaves us?
note: Best-before and resting-time numbers sit next to the answer as traps.

text: How long did Andrei estimate for building the subscription checkout?
note: Answer only in Russian; his English estimates for other tasks are traps.
